- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.6) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+5% from prior peak), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above recent high for next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤0.3) mid-period, model frequently underestimates; add 1–1.5% to forecast to account for mean reversion toward prior range.
- Model underperforms when sentiment is mixed (0.3–0.6) and price is volatile; use 3-day moving average of recent 18-day history as baseline for correction.
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome exceeds forecast by >1.5% across 3+ consecutive days, adjust downward by 0.5–1% per day until trend stabilizes.
- If sentiment history shows strong bullish momentum (e.g., 3+ consecutive 1.00 values), model often fails to capture full upside; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast for next 5 days.
